items.rootCause: After a recreated activity (wm density, display size, font size), the new React root starts on the live flow's screen only. app/+native-intent.tsx returns '/match' as the first URL, and expo-router builds a stack with that one route. The screens the player came through (Home, 'משחק חדש', 'סוג משחק') belonged to the old root's navigator, which is gone. So 'ביטול חיפוש' (MatchRoute onLeave → goBack) had no 'סוג משחק' to go back to. Without a recreation it goes back normally. The jest harness confirmed it: after the recreation, router.canGoBack() was false and the cancel did not reach 'סוג משחק'. On the phone it landed on 'משחק חדש' (the match route's own fallback, replace('/modes')). A second, smaller risk sits on the same path. On Android the first URL comes asynchronously, and expo-router's route info stays empty until its first change. The auth gate's once-per-root start can then read the path as Home, and resumeAtStart / roomToResume would push the same live screen a second time over the first.
items.fix: New apps/mobile/src/game/flowStack.ts. useFlowStack(), called from app/_layout.tsx, keeps the root's navigation state in module state on every change, so the state outlives the root. A root that started on a live flow is one that app/+native-intent.tsx marked with noteFlowStart(live). Once its container is ready, that root puts the old root's screens back under its own screen with resetRoot(restoredFlowState(...)). The new root's own route keeps its key and the navigator keys stay the same, so the search, game or room screen is not remounted and the search or seat is never left. Screens that start something on mount are never restored: game, match, friends/room, friends/join, room/[code], results. Nothing is restored if the old root was on another screen or had nothing under it. auth/useAuthGate.ts: a root that started on a live flow does not count as Home ('!startedOnLiveFlow()'), so it never pushes that screen a second time. No strings and no animations changed.
items.test: New apps/mobile/src/__tests__/recreatedFlowStack.test.tsx, through the real index.ts (latestRootOnly), the real +native-intent, the real useAuthGate and useFlowStack. Home → modes → game-type → match. Then a recreated root: it shows the search, canGoBack is true, the search screen mounts once (no remount), and 'ביטול חיפוש' lands on 'סוג משחק'. Back gives the modes, then Home. A root with nothing under way still starts on Home. Pure tests for restoredFlowState cover the keys kept, the screens never restored, and the cases where nothing is restored. With the resetRoot disabled, the main test fails ('Expected: true, Received: false' on canGoBack); I restored the line afterwards. Also passing: recreatedRootResume, rankedResume (unit and e2e), ranked.e2e, accounts.e2e, roomLinks.e2e, latestRoot, MatchScreen, nativeIntent, the auth suites and startupGraph.

The search screen comes back and the clock keeps counting. Tap 'ביטול חיפוש'. Expect the 'סוג משחק' screen (מהיר/רגיל/קשה, with מהיר chosen), not 'משחק חדש'. items.rootCause: Not found; no code change. What I measured: in fix12-RF8Y30L038L-cd-after2.png the box has sharp, square edges, at x 554–1025 and y 115–485 px. That is 139×110 dp at density 540: exactly the 'me' PlayerCard's frame, ending at the 16 dp game gutter. Inside it the background is 14 instead of 15 (one level darker). The ambient digits still show through it, and the card's own content (avatar, 'אני', '0') draws at full brightness. The first frame (cd-airplane-top-14s.png) shows the room screen's header ('חדר עם חברים' and '… מתוך 4') ghosted inside that same rectangle. The box goes away on the first tap, which re-renders the card. These are the signs of a stale window region over the ambient SurfaceView (AmbientCanvas.tsx: opaque, a SurfaceView on Android): the window's pixels there were not redrawn after the room screen went, until the card was invalidated. I checked these and ruled them out: the SelfReconnecting banner (full width) and scrim (full screen), card dimming (only when targeted or out, not on a reconnect), TargetFrame, and layout animations (none in the friends screens). PlayerCard's animated opacity and AvatarArt's renderToHardwareTextureAndroid are candidates, but I could not tie them to this rectangle from the code alone. QA saw it once. Without a reproduction I can't write a regression test that fails on the old code, so I made no speculative change.

items.rootCause: The screenshot (only the 'חדר עם חברים' title, a grey (muted) spinner with no text, no code, no seats, no back arrow) is exactly FriendsRoomScreen's 'gone' phase. The route draws it when there is no room (no friends session in the store) and no entry, or when the room's session is closed with no reason or problem to say: closeReason 'left', or 'gameOver' when the server disconnects 60 s after the game (closeAfterGameMs). The 'opening' spinner is accent-coloured and has text, so it is not that. 'gone' has no way out of its own. It only covers the route's one move away: the 'No room any more' effect sets left.current = true and calls goBack() once. If that move does not take the screen away, the spinner stays for good. Android back then left the app, so the room screen was the only screen in its stack. That happens on this phone's path: room 799709 was opened again in a recreated root (QA check E, wm density on Phone 1), then the game was replaced over it and the results pushed over the game. So 'משחק חדש' on the results would replace into a root-only /friends/room. Which exact tap or event put Phone 1 on the room screen, and why its one goBack went nowhere, cannot be shown without a JS log (QA could not reproduce it). So the cause of the move failing is not proven. The dead end itself is proven.

The header back arrow goes Home too. A normal leave, where goBack takes the screen away within a transition, never shows it: the timer is cleared on unmount, and any other phase resets it. It reuses the existing keys friends:closed.closed, actions.createRoom and actions.home, so no new strings and no animation. The change, together with Fix 1, also covers the likely way in: a recreated root now keeps the screens under the room (Home, 'משחק חדש'), so the room is no longer the only screen in the stack.

issues.problem: Item 3: the fix treats the symptom, not how the host got there. The most likely way in is a hidden /friends/room route underneath the game or results. Its 'No room any more' effect calls goBack() without checking that the route is focused, so it pops the screen the player is actually looking at (the results). useGoneWayOut only changes what shows next: about 60 s after the game, the host is still pulled off the results onto a room screen, which now reads 'החדר נסגר.' instead of a spinner.
issues.evidence: fixcheck-apk17.json: Phone 1 sat on the results, then '~2 min later' showed the room screen with no tap of its own, and Android back left the app, so the room was the only screen left. app/friends/room.tsx effect: `if (entry || left.current) return; if (room && (...)) return; left.current = true; goBack();` has no useIsFocused check. goBack() (screens/home/navigation.ts) does router.back(), which pops the top screen whoever calls it. In the old code a recreated root on '/friends/room' (QA check E) could get a second room screen: on Android expo-router's getInitialURL is a Promise, so the route info is empty and useSegments reads ''. useAuthGate then saw path '' as Home and called resumeAtStart, which runs router.push(liveFlowPath) (rankedResume.ts:260,304), giving [room#1, room#2]. room#2 is replaced by the game, room#1 stays underneath, and after closeAfterGameMs its goBack pops the screen above it. If goBack had reached the only screen in the stack it would replace('/'), so a 'move that went nowhere' fits this hidden route better than the fixer's explanation. The new test mocks goBack as a no-op, so it does not cover this.
issues.suggestion: Call goBack in the 'gone' effect only when this route is focused (useIsFocused, or navigation.isFocused()). When it is not focused, just set left.current. Add a route test with a stack of [friends/room, game, results]: closing the room must leave the results on top. Keep useGoneWayOut as a fallback.

issues.problem: The useAuthGate guard `!startedOnLiveFlow()` is probably what actually fixes the phone symptom in items 1 and 3: it stops the second live screen being pushed, and two stacked match screens explain 'cancel → משחק חדש' through match#1's replace('/modes'). But no test runs the Android path (async initial URL, empty segments). Turning the guard off fails no test.
issues.evidence: jest-expo's default preset is iOS, where expo-router's getInitialURL returns a string, so routeInfo is filled in at once and path reads 'match', not ''. recreatedFlowStack.test.tsx therefore never reaches the case where path === '' while startedOnLiveFlow() is true. I tried to run the test under jest-expo/android from a scratch config, but Babel failed to load the preset's setup.js, so this stays unverified.
issues.suggestion: Add a test that mocks the Android initial-URL path, or sets useSegments to [] for the recreated root's first render. It should check that resumeAtStart and roomToResume do not push a second '/match' or '/friends/room', and it should fail with the guard removed.

issues.problem: Item 2 (stale dark box over the 'אני' card after the countdown reconnect) is still open: there is no code change. The loop should treat it as not fixed, not as passed.
issues.evidence: Fixer status 'partial': 'Not found; no code change.' Its diagnosis (a window region over the AmbientCanvas SurfaceView, about the size of the PlayerCard, that was not redrawn) is a hypothesis that has not been checked on a phone.

issues.problem: Item 3: after 'צור חדר' from the stuck screen, the new room runs in a route instance whose refs are left over from before (left.current = true; toGame.current and goShownAt may be set). If the instance had gone into a game before (the hidden-route case), toGame.current = true blocks router.replace('/game') for the new room's game, and the stale goShownAt skips the GO hold.
issues.evidence: room.tsx: useGoneWayOut makes 'closed' → onCreateRoom → openRoom() in the same instance. The toGame effect returns early on `toGame.current`. `if (showsGo && goShownAt === null)` never resets. The 'gone' effect returns early on left.current, so a later close of the new room never moves away.
issues.suggestion: Reset toGame.current, left.current and goShownAt when openRoom succeeds. Or make the stuck 'צור חדר' do router.replace({pathname:'/friends/room', params:{create:'1'}}) so a fresh instance opens, as room/[code].tsx does.

issues.problem: Item 3: the fallback 'closed' StateView has `announce` on. If a room route that is not focused sits in 'gone' for 2 s, TalkBack can announce 'החדר נסגר.' over another screen. On the stuck screen, Android's hardware back still leaves the app when the room is the stack's only screen. Only the header arrow goes Home.
issues.evidence: FriendsRoomScreen 'closed' case: `announce`. useGoneWayOut runs whether or not the route is focused. No BackHandler for the 'closed' phase in room.tsx.
issues.suggestion: Turn the 'gone' phase into 'closed' only while the route is focused. Optionally send hardware back to onHome in the closed phase when router.canGoBack() is false.

issues.problem: Item 1 is checked only against expo-router's JS Stack in jest. The device path (react-native-screens on Fabric, resetRoot adding Home, 'משחק חדש' and 'סוג משחק' under an unchanged top screen, and the async initial URL on Android) has not been run.

On the phone, the restored state comes from getRootState() after the 'ready' event on an Android linking-resolved state. items.rootCause: There were two causes on the same path, and the review round confirmed both with tests. (1) After a recreated activity (wm density, display size, font size), the new React root starts on the live flow's screen only. app/+native-intent.tsx returns '/match', and the screens the player came through (Home, 'משחק חדש', 'סוג משחק') belonged to the old root's navigator, which is gone. So the cancel's goBack had no 'סוג משחק' to go back to. (2) This is the Android-only part that most likely matches the phone exactly. On Android, expo-router's getInitialURL is a Promise, so the new root's route info is empty when the auth gate's once-per-root start runs. useAuthGate read path '' as Home, and resumeAtStart pushed '/match' a second time over the first. The stack became [match#1, match#2]. On cancel, match#2 went back to match#1, which had no search and did its own fallback, replace('/modes'). That is the 'משחק חדש' QA saw. The new Android test proves it: with the guard removed, the search screen mounts 3 times instead of 2.

The new root's own route keeps its key, so the screen is not remounted. Screens that start something on mount (game, match, friends/room, friends/join, room/[code], results) are never restored. In auth/useAuthGate.ts, a root that started on a live flow does not count as Home (`&& !startedOnLiveFlow()`), so resumeAtStart and roomToResume never push that screen a second time. No strings and no animations changed.

items.rootCause: There were two causes on the same path, and the review round confirmed both with tests. (1) After a recreated activity (wm density, display size, font size), the new React root starts on the live flow's screen only. app/+native-intent.tsx returns '/match', and the screens the player came through (Home, 'משחק חדש', 'סוג משחק') belonged to the old root's navigator, which is gone. So the cancel's goBack had no 'סוג משחק' to go back to. (2) This is the Android-only part that most likely matches the phone exactly. On Android, expo-router's getInitialURL is a Promise, so the new root's route info is empty when the auth gate's once-per-root start runs. useAuthGate read path '' as Home, and resumeAtStart pushed '/match' a second time over the first. The stack became [match#1, match#2]. On cancel, match#2 went back to match#1, which had no search and did its own fallback, replace('/modes'). That is the 'משחק חדש' QA saw. The new Android test proves it: with the guard removed, the search screen mounts 3 times instead of 2.
items.fix: New apps/mobile/src/game/flowStack.ts with useFlowStack(), called from app/_layout.tsx. It keeps the root's navigation state in module state on every change. When a root starts on a live flow (marked by noteFlowStart in app/+native-intent.tsx), it puts the old root's screens back under its own with resetRoot once the container is ready. The new root's own route keeps its key, so the screen is not remounted. Screens that start something on mount (game, match, friends/room, friends/join, room/[code], results) are never restored. In auth/useAuthGate.ts, a root that started on a live flow does not count as Home (`&& !startedOnLiveFlow()`), so resumeAtStart and roomToResume never push that screen a second time. No strings and no animations changed.

The old replace used the Android stack fade, ANDROID_FADE_MS = 150. Before the mount also starts, the push now pays for the navigator render, a commit of FriendsGoFrame (2–4 AvatarArt SVG stacks, which the old path never drew) and afterFrames(1). The old Y, the time from GO! to the start of the mount, was 256–275 ms. The new figure is about X + ~50 ms, and X was 17–189 ms.
